key: Three several places of his birth they honour, in mid-air, in the heaven, and in the waters. Governing in the east of earthly regions, the seasons hath he stablished in their order.
s: In a hymn to Agni as a newborn infant, the verse counts his births; Sāyaṇa, on 1.95.3, reads the three as the fire beneath the ocean, the sun in heaven and the lightning, taking the first place as the sea and ‘the waters’ as mid-air.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.95.3, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 333253 (2022)

evidence.words: अस्याग्नेस्त्रीणि जन्मानि संभवन्ति । "समुद्रे अब्धौ वडवानलरूपेण “एकं जन्म । “दिवि द्युलोके आदित्यात्मना “एकम् । "अप्सु । आपः इति अन्तरिक्षनाम । अन्तरिक्षे वैद्युताग्निरूपेणैकम् ।
evidence.gloss: This Agni has three births: in the ocean, one birth, in the form of the submarine (mare’s) fire; in heaven, one, as the sun; in the waters: āpaḥ is a name of mid-air, so in mid-air, one, in the form of the lightning fire.

reason: Problem holds. Re-opened packet.js veda 12 --verse 1.95.3 (sa.wikisource revision 333253): the Sanskrit has samudre, divi, apsu in that order, which Griffith prints as ‘in mid-air, in the heaven, and in the waters’; Sāyaṇa glosses samudre as abdhau, the sea, with the submarine fire (vaḍavānala), divi as the sun, and apsu with āpaḥ iti antarikṣanāma, the lightning in mid-air. The old sentence named only the waters, so a reader matched the lightning to Griffith’s ‘mid-air’. CORRECTED to name both places in his terms: ‘taking the first place as the sea and ‘the waters’ as mid-air’. ‘Early’ dropped for the 45-word cap. Commentator, place, key, src and evidence unchanged; the evidence carries every part (sea, sun, lightning, waters as mid-air). verse.js ok (1.95.3, at [94,3]); entry-check ok (scratch/rev3-d12.json, 45 words); evidence re-found in the packet with the recheck normalisation.
